hook_text: Why was the peace treaty signed on 28 June 1919, in one particular room?
clip_script: Five years to the day after the shots at Sarajevo, German delegates walk into the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles, the room where the German Empire had been proclaimed in 1871. They were not allowed to negotiate. The terms: accept the guilt, pay reparations, keep an army of only one hundred thousand, give up Alsace and Lorraine, the Polish Corridor and every colony. South Africa receives South West Africa. Germans call it a Diktat. Was it too harsh, or not harsh enough? Historians still argue.
visual_style: A whiteboard Hall of Mirrors with a treaty on a table, then a map of Germany shrinking as territories and colonies are coloured away.
pacing: Builds from the setting to the terms to the debate.
